headline: Earnings top guidance despite a GAAP operating loss
summary_short: Robert Half's Q2 2026 revenue fell 2.4% year-over-year to $1,336.4 million, but net income of $26.3 million ($0.26/share) topped the midpoint of management's guidance even as a deferred-compensation reclassification pushed GAAP operating income to a $62.3 million loss.
summary_long: Q2 2026 revenue fell 2% y/y (3% adjusted) to $1.336B; contract talent and Protiviti declined while permanent placement grew 2.5% adjusted y/y, its third straight quarter of sequential adjusted growth. Reported gross margin fell to 35.5% from 37.2% y/y (adjusted: 37.2% vs 38.1%), driven mainly by Protiviti margin compression. GAAP operating income swung to a $62.3M loss from $1.5M y/y, fully explained by a $100.9M non-cash deferred-compensation-trust reclassification that nets to zero against non-operating income; adjusted operating income fell to $38.6M from $59.2M. Net income was $26.3M ($0.26/share), down from $41.0M ($0.41/share) y/y but up from $13.8M ($0.14/share) q/q. Cash rose to $324.7M from $278.4M q/q. No new guidance stated.

drivers.explanation: CEO Waddell says hiring demand continues to improve and market conditions are increasingly supportive, with talent solutions posting a third straight quarter of sequential adjusted revenue growth even as y/y comparisons stay negative.

Decline driven by continued softness in contract finance/accounting and administrative/customer-support staffing, partially offset by technology growth and 2.5% adjusted y/y growth in permanent placement.
Compression traces mainly to Protiviti, whose adjusted gross margin fell to 18.5% from 22.3% y/y; talent-solutions segment margins were roughly flat y/y.

Swing to a reported loss is fully explained by a $100.9M reclassification of deferred-compensation-trust investment gains into operating expense, an item the release says is completely offset by an equal non-operating gain.
Not separately explained beyond the adjusted operating income decline ($38.6M vs $59.2M y/y); release gives no additional cause for the net-income drop.
